title: Rotation Schema
strapline: Wheels, taps, whisks and their own dizzy spinning bodies — the child in love with everything that turns.
intent: Recognise rotation as a schema — a fascination with round things, turning things, spinning bodies and circular motion.
Understand the learning inside it: cause and effect, how mechanisms work, circles and going-round in space.
Read the endless tap-turning, wheel-spinning and body-whirling as research into how the world rotates.
Build the hand strength and twisting control that later manage lids, taps, keys and toothpaste.
Feed the whole-body version too — rolling, spinning and going round give powerful vestibular input.
implementation: Offer things that turn: wheels, cogs, whisks, egg-beaters, spinning tops, nuts and bolts, jar lids, a salad spinner, a real tap on a water tray.
Provide circular movement for the body — a roundabout, ribbons to whirl, space to spin, hills to roll down.
Name the schema alongside them ('round and round the wheel goes — you made it spin!').
Add mark-making that rotates — circular scribbles, spin-art, painting round and round on a turntable.
Keep spinning bodies safe with soft space and supervision, and check any bolts and mechanisms are secure and sized safely.
key_questions: What made the wheel go round?
Can you turn the lid — which way does it go?
How does it feel when you spin round and round?
The whisk goes round and round — what happens to the bubbles?
Can your crayon go round in a big circle?

impact.text: A child turns whisks, taps, lids and wheels, discovering they can make things spin — early cause and effect.
Toddlers twist and turn nuts, bolts and lids, hands strengthening for taps, keys and fastenings to come.
Children roll, spin and whirl their whole bodies on purpose, exploring circular movement and balance.
Round-and-round marks appear as toddlers scribble circles and swirl paint on a turning surface.

enhancements: A tinker tray of nuts, bolts and jar lids for twisting on and off.
A water tray with a real tap, a whisk and a salad spinner.
Spin-art or a turntable for round-and-round mark-making.
Cogs and gears on a board, plus wheeled vehicles to spin and roll.
Ribbons and scarves for whirling, and a safe soft space for spinning bodies.

playing_exploring: The child seeks out everything that turns, testing wheels, taps and their own spinning self.
Rotation is explored with hands, tools and whole-body movement.
active_learning: Toddlers turn the same lid or wheel over and over, refining the twist until it works.
creating_thinking: Children link their own action to the spin — I turned it, it went round — and try to make it happen again.
